name: South Sumatra
summary_text: On 19 July 2026 Palembang's city government announced it was preparing a regulation rejecting LGBT, presented as local follow-through on Presidential Regulation (Perpres) No. 111 of 2025 on the national defence policy 2025-2029, which lists the 'spread of LGBTQ culture' among non-military threats; Mayor Ratu Dewa made the announcement in the courtyard of the Grand Mosque. The regulation remains in preparation, not enacted, with no specified penalty; no enforcement event is documented for this province. South Sumatra is one of the eight provinces analysed in OutRight's discriminatory-regulation mapping, and its neighbour Lampung saw a documented Satpol PP raid on three transwomen (November 2018) - the Sumatran belt is where local enforcement is consolidating. The deviation from the national score is small and below it, similar to South Sulawesi (0.13). The Perpres 111/2025 framing elevates local anti-LGBT measures from moral panic to national-defence doctrine - the August 2026 ABC reporting links the 'rule that deems them a threat' to a wave of street attacks on trans women, though it cautions the trend cannot yet be confirmed - but without an enacted local penalty the traveler-facing risk here remains prospective. It sits above West Sumatra (0.11), which has a live bylaw with specified sanctions.

sources.title: Pemkot Palembang Siapkan Regulasi Penolakan LGBT - RRI.co.id
sources.claim_summary: RRI Palembang (19 July 2026): Mayor Ratu Dewa announces from the Grand Mosque courtyard that the city government is preparing an anti-LGBT 'rejection' regulation, explicitly framed as implementation of Perpres No. 111/2025 on general state defence policy 2025-2029, which classifies the spread of LGBTQ culture as a non-military threat alongside terrorism and trafficking.

OutRight Action International, 'Creeping Criminalisation': the mapping of discriminatory regional regulations in eight Indonesian provinces includes South Sumatra, evidencing the province's place in the regional-bylaw belt that drafts like Palembang's extend.

sources.title: Attacks on trans women in Indonesia did not suddenly appear. Here's what's behind them - ABC News
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (not cached; ABC served no content to the fetcher); per the research dossier this ABC News report (15 August 2026) covers men attacking trans women in Indonesia after the rule that deems them a threat, citing Arus Pelangi's record of 28 attacks in 2024 rising to 66 in 2025, while cautioning it is unclear whether the Bogor wave represents a genuine overall increase.
